name: Romania
seoTitle: History of Romania: Carpathian Fortress, Blue-Yellow-Red Tricolor, and 1918 Great Union
metaDescription: Discover the detailed history of Romania. Explore the Dacian kingdom, Vlad the Impaler, the 1918 Great Union, the Carpathian Mountains, and the Romanian tricolor.
mapFormation:
Spanning 238,397 square kilometers in Southeastern Europe centered on the arc of the Carpathian Mountains and the lower Danube River delta along the Black Sea, Romania (România) is the twelfth-largest country in the European Union.

The territory was inhabited in antiquity by the Dacians under King Decebalus before being conquered by Roman Emperor Trajan in 106 CE, leading to the Daco-Roman ethnogenesis and Latin Romance language of modern Romanians. In the Middle Ages, three principalities emerged: Wallachia, Moldavia, and Transylvania.

In 1859, the personal union of Wallachia and Moldavia under Prince Alexandru Ioan Cuza created the United Principalities. Full sovereign independence from the Ottoman Empire was achieved during the 1877–1878 War of Independence. Following World War I, the Great Union of December 1, 1918 (Marea Unire) united Transylvania, Bessarabia, and Bukovina with the Kingdom of Romania in Alba Iulia, establishing modern frontiers.
flagHistory:
The national flag of Romania—the Tricolorul—features three equal vertical bands of cobalt blue (hoist), chrome yellow (middle), and vermilion red (fly), formally adopted by the Provisional Government on June 26, 1848, during the Wallachian Revolution.

The three colors combine the traditional heraldic banners of the Romanian principalities: Blue for Wallachia (symbolizing liberty and the blue skies), Yellow for Moldavia (symbolizing justice and golden wheat fields), and Red for Transylvania (symbolizing fraternity and patriotic blood shed in defense of the realm). Following the 1989 Revolution, the communist coat of arms was removed from the center, restoring the pure historic tricolor.
freedomStory:
Romania's sovereign freedom is rooted in the 1848 Wallachian Revolution and the heroic events of the 1989 Romanian Revolution.

On December 1, 1918, over 100,000 delegates gathered at the National Assembly in Alba Iulia to proclaim the unification of Transylvania with Romania (celebrated annually as Great Union Day / Ziua Marii Uniri).

In December 1989, popular protests against the totalitarian regime of Nicolae Ceaușescu erupted in Timișoara and Bucharest. Courageous citizens cut the communist crest out of the center of Romanian flags, creating the famous 'flag with a hole'. On December 22, 1989, the dictatorship was overthrown, establishing constitutional democracy under the 1991 Constitution. Romania joined NATO in 2004 and the European Union in 2007.
challenges: As a major industrial and agricultural economy and NATO's Black Sea strategic anchor, Romania is accelerating national infrastructure projects. Foremost priorities include completing the A7 and A8 Moldavia highway corridors, expanding nuclear power units at Cernavodă, and developing offshore natural gas reserves in the Black Sea (Neptun Deep).

faqs.question: What is celebrated on December 1 in Romania?
faqs.answer: December 1 is Great Union Day (Ziua Marii Uniri), Romania's National Day, commemorating the 1918 assembly in Alba Iulia that unified Transylvania, Bessarabia, and Bukovina with the Kingdom of Romania.

faqs.question: Why is the Romanian language unique in Eastern Europe?
faqs.answer: Romanian is the only Eastern Romance language, descending from Vulgar Latin spoken in the Roman province of Dacia, making it closely related to Italian, Spanish, French, and Portuguese.

timeline.event: Emperor Trajan conquers Dacia, initiating Romanization and the Romanian language.
Alexandru Ioan Cuza unifies Wallachia and Moldavia into the United Principalities.
Romania proclaims sovereign independence from the Ottoman Empire on May 9.
The Great Union of Alba Iulia on December 1 unites all historic Romanian lands.
The December Revolution topples the communist regime, restoring democracy.
Romania officially joins the European Union.
